sources.title: Institut Tshakapesh, La Nation innue
sources.note: Community institution page, headings La Nation innue and Les 11 communautes innues du Quebec et du Labrador: Nitassinan, seasonal mobility, lack of a fixed frontier, community diversity, and living transmission.

sources.title: Parks Canada, Meshikamau-shipu Travel Route National Historic Event
sources.note: Paragraphs 20 to 29: 330-kilometre route, active and ancestral camps, portages, births and burials, family gatherings, travel, distant stone, oral history, and continuing use.

sources.title: Parks Canada, Kameshtashtan National Historic Site
sources.note: Paragraphs 21 to 27, 35 to 47, and heritage value 67 to 74: ancient camps, family landscape, caribou crossings, caches, hearths, foods, travel, and current use.

sources.title: Frederick A. Schwarz, In the Eagle's Nest: Archaeological Investigations in the Mistassini Lake Area
sources.note: Archaeology in Newfoundland and Labrador 1997, paragraphs 18 to 55, 60 to 112, and 118 to 148: survey limits, visibility, trade, recent camp inventories, and uncertain precontact components.

sources.title: Pierre Bibeau, Phase 2 Report on a Heritage Study for the Utshimassit Community Relocation Project
sources.note: Archaeology in Newfoundland and Labrador 1996, introduction paragraphs 9 to 14 and site discussion: government-directed 1967 settlement, water and sewer problems, and older archaeological attribution.

sources.title: Andronowski-Brake et al., Labrador Beothuk: A reconsideration of the Point Revenge complex
sources.note: North American Archaeologist 47.3-4, pages 59 to 89; abstract paragraphs 32 to 36 tests ancestry hypotheses and supports a relationship with Beothuk rather than silent assignment to Innu.

sources.title: Peter Armitage, The Innu (The Montagnais-Naskapi)
sources.note: Community-hosted book. Printed pages 13 to 19 introduce identity and older archaeology; pages 66 to 73 describe twentieth-century camps, household work, foods, and gatherings. Used only as dated comparison.

sources.title: Innu Round Table Secretariat, A Guide to Fostering Innu Culture
sources.note: Community health staff guide, printed pages 3 to 9: historical disruption, extended family, collective childrearing, learning through participation, and flexible work roles. Retrospective/current evidence is marked.

sources.title: Peter Armitage and Innu Traditional Knowledge Committee, Innu Environmental Knowledge of the Mishta-shipu
sources.note: Report to Innu Nation, 2007. Printed pages 64 to 67, section 9 Nutshimiu-natukun: country medicine, documentation limits, knowledge governance, relative strength, and landscape relationships.

sources.title: Nametau innu, Material Culture
sources.note: Musee regional de la Cote-Nord community knowledge site, paragraphs 112 to 121: archaeological stone tools, organic preservation limits, later photographs, shelters, snowshoes, canoes, and sleds.

sources.title: Nametau innu, Archaeology on Innu Territory
sources.note: Paragraphs 112 to 130: Cote-Nord site counts, Sainte-Marguerite River excavations, four-millennia use, passage sites, structures, and diverse stone sources.

sources.title: Nametau innu, First Contact
sources.note: Paragraphs 112 to 121: Cabot in 1497, Breton fisheries documented in 1506, Cartier meeting Breton crews in 1534, and cautious inference about later Innu-European contact.

sources.title: Innu Language Lessons, Nitassinan
sources.note: Current lesson heading and activity text: the Roman-orthography form Nitassinan with the English translation Our territory and east/west dialect controls.

sources.title: Natural Resources Canada, Innu-aimun audio for place names in Labrador
sources.note: Official page: research beginning in 1976, nearly 1,200 names, almost 500 official names, over 400 audio files, and associated place histories shared by Innu Nation.

sources.title: Mamu Tshishkutamashutau Innu Education, About MTIE
sources.note: Current Innu education authority page: established 2009, two community schools, Innu-selected trustees, and education honoring language, land, culture, and community goals.

sources.title: Government of Canada, Impact Evaluation of the Labrador Innu Comprehensive Healing Strategy
sources.note: Final evaluation report, 2009, printed pages 7 to 10 and 18 to 27: community healing, health programs, relocation, clean water, indoor plumbing, and evidence limitations.

sources.title: Gouvernement du Quebec, Naskapi
sources.note: Official current profile, sections Population and territory, Language, and History: distinct Naskapi Nation, Kawawachikamach, iyuw iyimuun, caribou mobility, and modern institutions.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Snowshoes, catalog 13/3080
sources.note: Object record NMAI_142572: Montagnais Innu attribution, Labrador, collected 1924, wood and hide thong, carved and plaited techniques.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Cup and pin game, catalog 13/3201
sources.note: Object record NMAI_142797: Montagnais Innu attribution, Labrador, collected 1924, animal bone, hide thong, deer tail, incised and perforated.

sources.title: Mamu Tshishkutamashutau Innu Education, Innu curriculum resources
sources.note: Current curriculum catalogue sections for Innu-aimun activities, beginner lessons, school vocabulary, early literacy, spelling, typing, and Innu social studies.

sources.title: Government of Canada, Labrador Innu Land Claims Agreement-in-Principle
sources.note: Chapter 22, Part 22.9 Archaeology, sections 22.9.1 to 22.9.4: proposed artifact transfer, burial protection, consultation, conservation, and reburial responsibilities.

sources.title: Nametau innu, Food from the Caribou
sources.note: Community museum teaching page, paragraphs 91 to 103 and 160 to 175: caribou food knowledge, guest portions, bone fat, birch-bark storage, respect, and explicit elder-to-youth transmission context.
